M7j acceptance: mixed CSV and OGC fixtures derive deterministic candidates in original global fetch order and share explicit count and aggregate reserved-byte admission; dry run produces identical request, identity, and one-row-per-distribution status facts without host or provider work; live requests run sequentially with unique child scopes and at most one physical attempt each; one redacted CSV transport failure does not prevent the later OGC request; a missing OGC symbol charges no transport or bytes; an invalid OGC page becomes one charged parse-failure row without discarding CSV successes; successful status rows map one-to-one to handler-specific compact results; whole-object validation rebuilds M7i and rejects forged candidate, plan, scope, CSV data, OGC body/result, status, byte, index, error, count, or metadata facts; and M7j plus public gx_fetch() remain unexported.

M7k acceptance: one WQP Result fixture rebinds to its exact M7d held reservation and deterministic service/profile/site/characteristic/time request snapshot without host work; ambiguous endpoints, extra or duplicate query fields, non-CSV intent, and partial-day filters fail closed; invocation checks the dataRetrieval::importWQP symbol before DNS, then performs exactly one bounded request with no retry, redirect, cache, or attribute follow-up; the external character parser must match the independently strict parsed table; missing-symbol failure charges no attempt or bytes, while transport and parser failures produce one typed redacted terminal row and do not prevent later OGC work; compact retained bytes, schema, table, parse, scope, execution, and attempt identities fully revalidate; shared dry-run and live scheduling now orders CSV, WQP, and OGC candidates globally under one count/byte admission pass; forged plan/result/ledger/status/metadata facts fail closed; and M7k plus public gx_fetch() remain unexported.

M7l acceptance: one EDR position fixture rebinds to its exact M7d held reservation and deterministic base/collection/point/parameter/time/CRS84/ CoverageJSON request snapshot without host work; foreign paths, fragments, duplicate or extra query fields, invalid points, ambiguous parameters, and conflicting datetime/CRS/format values fail closed; invocation verifies edr4r >= 0.1.1, edr_position, and covjson_to_tibble before DNS and then performs exactly one bounded request with no retry, redirect, cache, or page follow; the external offline normalizer must exactly match the strict bounded PointSeries table; missing capability charges no attempt or bytes, while transport and parse failures produce one typed redacted terminal row and do not prevent later OGC work; compact retained bytes, schema, table, parse, scope, execution, and attempt identities fully revalidate without the optional package; shared dry-run and live scheduling now orders CSV, WQP, EDR, and OGC candidates globally under one count/byte admission pass; forged plan/result/ ledger/status/metadata facts fail closed; and M7l plus public gx_fetch() remain unexported.

M7m acceptance: one current USGS continuous fixture rebinds to its exact M7d held reservation and deterministic host/version/collection/site/parameter/time/ property/representation/limit request snapshot without host work; foreign or latest/daily paths, fragments, duplicate or extra query fields, ambiguous site or parameter values, and conflicting inherited options fail closed; invocation verifies dataRetrieval >= 2.7.22 and exported read_waterdata_continuous() capability before DNS and then performs exactly one bounded request with no retry, redirect, cache, or page follow; the strict fixed GeoJSON table preserves measurement strings and binds site, parameter, RFC 3339 times, counts, and truncation; missing capability charges no attempt or bytes, while transport and parse failures produce one typed redacted terminal row and do not prevent later OGC work; compact retained bytes, schema, table, parse, scope, execution, and attempt identities fully revalidate without the optional package; shared dry-run and live scheduling now orders CSV, WQP, EDR, USGS continuous, and OGC candidates globally under one count/byte admission pass; forged plan/result/ledger/status/metadata facts fail closed; and M7m plus public gx_fetch() remain unexported.

M7n acceptance: one current USGS daily fixture rebinds to its exact M7d held reservation and deterministic host/version/collection/site/parameter/statistic/ local-date/property/representation/limit request snapshot without host work; foreign, continuous, or latest-daily paths, fragments, duplicate or extra query fields, ambiguous site/parameter/statistic values, and conflicting inherited options fail closed; invocation verifies dataRetrieval >= 2.7.22 and exported read_waterdata_daily() before DNS and performs exactly one bounded request with no retry, redirect, cache, or page follow; the strict fixed GeoJSON table preserves measurement strings, local Date observations, UTC modification times, and unknown missing match counts; missing capability charges no attempt or bytes, while transport and parse failures do not prevent later OGC work; compact retained evidence fully revalidates without the optional package; shared dry-run and live scheduling orders all six handler families globally; forged plan/result/ledger/status/metadata facts fail closed; and M7n plus public gx_fetch() remain unexported.

M7 closure acceptance: gx_fetch_plan() binds the built-in registry and budgets without provider work; gx_fetch() accepts only sequential execution, provides a deterministic no-host dry run, and returns gx_fetched 0.1.0 with one status row per distribution, one handler-native payload row per success, and the validated M7n provenance. Public projection or nested provenance forgery fails closed. Latest/legacy providers, other EDR queries, pagination, registration, and serialization/replay are explicitly deferred enhancements, not M8 gates.

M8 — Harmonization

gx_harmonize(fetched, target_units = gx_target_units())

Map variables by reviewed URI alignments. Unit conversions use directed, reviewed rows with from_unit_uri, to_unit_uri, scale, offset, dimension, source, and review date:

converted_value = original_value * scale + offset

This supports affine conversions such as Fahrenheit→Celsius. Unknown/ambiguous mappings remain unchanged and harmonized = FALSE; never infer solely from a label. Preserve raw values/units and conversion rule IDs.

Acceptance: forward/reverse affine and multiplicative tests, incompatible-dimension rejection, missing/ambiguous mappings, qualifiers, duplicate timestamps, timezone normalization, and lossless access to raw payloads.

The implemented M8a–M8e checkpoint is deliberately conservative. It accepts the frozen gx_fetched 0.1.0 contract and extracts only the strict EDR position and current USGS continuous/daily time-series schemas plus exact filtered WQP Result rows with a reviewed timezone code and explicitly mapped direct-CSV tables or OGC API Features properties. Exactly one catalog parameter must provide the variable and unit URI, and the native unit label must exactly corroborate the catalog label before the URI can select a reviewed rule. WQP additionally requires one exact requested characteristic and site, exact catalog/native characteristic agreement, and strict date/time plus one active EPA TimeZoneCode for every row. The reported code selects its reviewed fixed offset; geography and daylight-saving rules are never inferred. Daily dates become UTC midnight without sorting or deduplication. Unfiltered, mixed-characteristic, unknown-timezone, or incomplete WQP results remain native-only. A direct CSV additionally requires an embedded identity-bound mapping for one planned distribution, strict UTC timestamp text, exact mapped columns, explicit missing tokens, and exactly one catalog variable. An OGC API Features result requires the equivalent embedded property mapping; generated feature identifiers and geometry cannot be mapped to observation roles, and the planned distribution remains the source of site identity. Unmapped or schema-incompatible CSV and OGC API Features remain native-only. Their native payloads remain available through the exact embedded fetched object. The normalized call is capped at 1,000,000 rows and performs no host or provider work. See ADRs 0036–0040.

M9 — Package, report, snapshot, and replay

gx_package(x, dir, timeseries = c("csv", "parquet"),
           keep_raw = TRUE, overwrite = FALSE, report = FALSE,
           frictionless = FALSE)
gx_report(x, output = NULL)
gx_snapshot(x, dir, time = NULL, fetch = TRUE, report = TRUE, ...)
gx_replay(manifest, dir = NULL, refresh = FALSE, ...)

x may be a catalog, fetched object, or harmonized object. Package creation is catalog-only capable. Report rendering happens before final manifest/resource hashes are written.

Suggested layout:

<dir>/
  datapackage.json
  manifest.json
  requests.csv
  catalog/sites.gpkg
  catalog/datasets.csv
  catalog/problems.csv
  catalog/fetch_status.csv
  reference/reference.gpkg
  data/observations.csv|parquet
  data/raw/...
  report/snapshot_report.html

The manifest distinguishes:

  • recipe replay: rerun the same procedure against current services;
  • snapshot verification: verify stored resource SHA-256 values and request ledger offline.

It does not promise identical future row counts. Manifest fields include schema/package versions, canonical AOI recipe and geometry, effective options, endpoint and hydrologic vintage, query/registry/vocabulary hashes, request/final URLs, request/body/content hashes, ETag/Last-Modified where present, timestamps, cache origin, handler versions, resource hashes, source licences, completeness, and session details.

gx_replay(refresh = TRUE) re-executes the recipe. refresh = FALSE verifies/loads stored assets and errors if required assets are absent. Custom non-package handlers are reported as non-replayable.

The implemented M9a verifier is deliberately narrow. Public gx_snapshot_verify(dir) wraps that exact substrate and reads only <dir>/manifest.json, validates the full manifest-v1 shape with mandatory package code, and treats planned replay fields as inert metadata. It extracts the AOI into M6b’s exact aoi to catalog fragment so identifier or custom-geometry identity is independently re-established without executing the recipe. The embedded request array is shape-validated as the authoritative ledger; request hashes and historical claims are not recomputed.

M9a inventories a closed snapshot tree before and after verification. Resource paths use bounded portable ASCII POSIX names; aliases, prefix collisions, symlinks, hard-link aliases, special files, undeclared entries, unreadable directories, and directories outside declared resource prefixes fail closed. Declared resources remain opaque bytes and are hashed in bytewise path order under 1 GiB per-resource and aggregate ceilings. A missing optional resource is visible but allowed; a missing required resource or any present size/hash/type mismatch aborts. The verifier makes no network, DNS, resource-parser, decompression, cache, repair, or write call.

This proves internal consistency relative to an unsigned manifest, not authenticity, historical request provenance, licence truth, or protection from coordinated replacement of both manifest and resources. Public gx_replay(refresh = FALSE) is supplied by M9ab for only the exact fixed catalog-snapshot and package loading profiles. It does not interpret a Frictionless profile or execute the stored recipe.

M9c publishes only this integrity-evidence boundary. Its validated gx_snapshot_verification result binds the normalized manifest, rebound AOI, request count, expected resources, observed size/hash evidence, optional absences, manifest SHA-256, and verification time. It performs no resource loading or replay and makes the unsigned-consistency limitation explicit under ADR 0041.

The internal M9b checkpoint adds creation-only catalog snapshot writing without exporting its serializer and publication seams. It accepts only M6c catalogs, revalidates immediately before serialization, writes deterministic redacted UTF-8 CSV resources and manifest-v1 in a sibling staging tree, validates the exact manifest bytes, verifies the closed tree through M9a, and publishes only to an absent destination before verifying again. Its manifest is explicitly non-replayable. Frictionless metadata, deterministic GeoPackage bytes, overwrite ownership, loading, signatures, refresh, fetch/harmonize resources, and reports remain gated under ADR 0019.

M9d exposes that exact catalog-only boundary as gx_snapshot(x, dir, fetch = FALSE, report = FALSE, overwrite = FALSE). Only a valid gx_catalog and scalar false flags are accepted; fetched or harmonized inputs and any request for fetch, report, or overwrite fail before filesystem publication. The exact gx_snapshot result binds the normalized destination path, final M9c verification evidence, fixed scope metadata, and a deterministic snapshot identifier. Its embedded verification must describe the four M9b resources, end at the catalog stage, and remain explicitly non-replayable. This does not add loading, resource parsing, Frictionless acceptance, authenticity, or a fetched-data packaging claim under ADR 0042.

M9e adds an internal request-export loading prerequisite. It recognizes only the exact M9b serialization and non-replayable profile, re-derives canonical requests.csv bytes from the normalized manifest ledger, requires exact byte equality under a 64 MiB loading ceiling, converts that ledger to the exact typed catalog request table, and re-verifies the complete tree afterward. The result binds the typed rows, manifest hash, resource hash, count, and deterministic export identity. Catalog sites, datasets, and problems remain opaque because their redacted CSV views are not losslessly reversible into live catalog identities. M9e adds no public loader or replay claim under ADR 0043.

M9f publishes that exact request-ledger substrate as gx_snapshot_requests(dir). The validated gx_snapshot_request_export result binds its normalized snapshot path, typed rows, count, manifest hash, request-resource hash, and deterministic export identity. Its public print contract states that the evidence proves unsigned offline consistency rather than historical truth or authenticity. Sites, datasets, problems, and all non-catalog resources remain unloaded under ADR 0044.

M9g adds the internal loading prerequisite for catalog/sites.csv, catalog/datasets.csv, and catalog/problems.csv. It recognizes only the fixed writer declarations, reads at most 64 MiB under resource-specific row and global column/field ceilings, parses every cell as character data, and requires the table to reserialize byte-for-byte to the quote-all UTF-8 LF input. The complete snapshot is verified before and after loading, and exact evidence binds the resource, normalized path, table, dimensions, manifest/resource hashes, and deterministic identity. Blank fields remain blank; WKT, JSON, timestamps, logicals, and redacted identities remain uninterpreted under ADR 0045.

M9h combines the three M9g tables with M9f request evidence and final M9c verification as an exact gx_snapshot_catalog_view. It types only fixed writer-declared fields: bounded CRS84 point WKT, UTC timestamps, true/false logicals, and canonical conforms-to JSON string arrays. Every other redacted or blank string remains unchanged, the original character-table evidence is retained, and whole-object validation re-derives every typed projection. Scope metadata explicitly declares preserved empty strings, non-reconstructed identities, and non-replayability under ADR 0046.

M9i publishes that exact value object through gx_snapshot_catalog_view(dir). The public name, documentation, and print contract identify the result as a typed redacted snapshot view rather than a live gx_catalog. The wrapper repeats whole-object validation and preserves M9h’s fixed-profile recognition, loading budgets, canonical evidence, before-and-after verification, offline and read-only behavior, and non-replayability under ADR 0047. It does not restore discarded URI components, distinguish exported blanks from original missing values, authenticate the unsigned manifest, or load fetched or harmonized resources.

M9j adds the internal package-input admission prerequisite. Exact catalog inputs are self-contained. Because the frozen gx_fetched and gx_harmonized contracts do not embed the complete originating catalog, those stages require an explicit catalog and re-derive its fetch-plan source before requiring exact AOI, dataset hash, completeness, truncation, contract-version, and row-count agreement. The exact gx_package_input result retains catalog, fetched, native payload, and harmonized evidence; binds the four canonical redacted catalog projections, plan/status/result identities, reviewed harmonization determinants, counts, stage, and a deterministic input identity; and revalidates the full lineage under ADR 0048. It performs no serialization, write, publication, optional-format, loading, report, refresh, or replay work.

M9k derives exact in-memory bytes from one M9j input. The fixed profile always contains the four canonical redacted catalog CSVs. Fetched and harmonized stages add canonical fetch-status and native-index CSVs plus one resource for each successful result: exact retained provider response bytes when M7 declares them available, or canonical quote-all UTF-8 LF CSV for strict direct-CSV tables where no original body was retained. Harmonized stages also add canonical redacted observations and harmonized-resource CSVs. Every path-sorted entry binds path, role, format, media type, byte count, SHA-256, dimensions, and result/distribution/handler identities; the bundle re-derives all bytes during validation. The in-memory profile is capped at 10,000 resources, 128 MiB per resource, 256 MiB aggregate, and five million CSV fields under ADR 0049. It performs no filesystem write, staging, publication, manifest construction, loading, optional-format, report, refresh, or replay work.

M9l publishes one exact M9k bundle through a private sibling staging tree. It writes only the bundle’s already-determined resources plus a deterministic manifest-v1 document, verifies the closed stage through M9a, atomically renames it only to an absent destination, and verifies the exposed tree again. The manifest ends at package, binds the M9j input and M9k bundle identities, records actual selected fetch-handler order and harmonization target units, and declares its request ledger catalog_only. Fetched package manifests are explicitly non-replayable because the frozen fetched contract does not retain a complete provider request ledger. The exact internal publication object binds the source stage, normalized path, bundle, final verification, fixed creation-only metadata, and publication identity. Pre-publication failures remove only the writer-owned stage; failures after atomic exposure never delete the target under ADR 0050. No public API, overwrite, loading, Frictionless, optional-format, report, refresh, authenticity, or replay claim is added.

M9m exposes that exact chain as gx_package(x, dir, catalog = NULL, timeseries = "csv", keep_raw = TRUE, overwrite = FALSE). Exact catalog inputs are self-contained; fetched and harmonized inputs require the explicit source catalog and pass M9j’s full AOI and dataset-lineage rebinding before serialization. The initial public profile admits only deterministic CSV/raw resources, preserves every provider body retained by M7, and refuses overwrite. It returns a compact exact gx_package object binding the normalized path, source stage, final M9a evidence, fixed scope, M9j input identity, M9k bundle identity, and package identity. Package loading is a separate boundary under ADR 0052; Arrow/Parquet, Quarto, Frictionless metadata, reports, authenticity, refresh, and replay remain outside the creation contract under ADR 0051.

M9n exposes gx_package_load(dir) for the exact M9m writer profile. It verifies the closed tree before reading, applies the M9k per-resource and aggregate byte ceilings, checks file identity around every read, rebinds each raw vector to its manifest size and SHA-256, and verifies the whole tree again. The returned gx_package_loaded object retains the source stage, final M9a evidence, path-sorted role and format inventory, exact named resource bytes, fixed scope metadata, and deterministic load identity. CSV resources are not parsed and native payloads remain opaque. Loading is read-only, offline, unsigned, non-Frictionless, and non-replayable and does not reconstruct gx_catalog, gx_fetched, or gx_harmonized.

M9o exposes gx_package_tables(dir) over the exact M9n result. Every CSV resource is parsed only from its already verified in-memory bytes through the bounded bytewise parser, remains character-only, and must serialize exactly back to its original quote-all UTF-8/LF resource. The returned gx_package_tables object embeds the full M9n evidence, binds every table path, resource SHA-256, row count, and column count, and leaves native raw resources opaque. It does not infer storage types or semantics, reconstruct a live workflow object, authorize overwrite, or broaden authenticity, Frictionless, refresh, or replay claims under ADR 0053.

M9p adds an internal typed package-hydration substrate over the exact M9o result. It reuses M9h’s redacted catalog typing, rebinds requests.csv to the manifest ledger, and applies only explicit fixed integer, double, logical, and UTC timestamp conversions to package-owned fetch-status, native-index, observation, and harmonized-resource tables. Provider-native CSV tables remain character-only and raw payloads remain opaque. The exact value object retains the complete M9o evidence and re-derives every projection during validation; it does not reconstruct live workflow objects or add a public API, overwrite, authenticity, Frictionless, refresh, or replay claim under ADR 0054.

M9q exposes that exact substrate through gx_package_hydrate(dir). The public wrapper returns the fully revalidated M9p object and its complete M9o/M9n evidence, with typed package-owned catalog, fetch-index, and harmonization tables selected by source stage. Provider-native CSV tables remain character-only and raw provider resources remain opaque. Its documentation and print contract identify the view as redacted, read-only, non-replayable, and distinct from a reconstructed live workflow object under ADR 0055.

M9r adds an internal owned-package replacement substrate. The existing destination must first pass complete M9a verification and M9m fixed-profile recognition; that exact manifest acts as the content-bound ownership marker. The new M9k bundle is independently published and verified at a sibling path before the prior tree is moved to a sibling backup. Installation and final verification failures synchronously restore and re-verify the prior package. If restoration or cleanup cannot complete, typed errors retain and report the recovery paths and whether replacement committed. Successful evidence binds both manifest generations, the new bundle, fixed rollback policy, and a deterministic replacement identity. The portable contract detects races but cannot promise crash-atomic directory exchange under ADR 0056.

M9s exposes that substrate through gx_package(..., overwrite = TRUE). The destination must already be an intact fixed-writer package; missing, arbitrary, malformed, or corrupt paths remain untouched. The public gx_package v0.2 evidence distinguishes creation from replacement through its mode, status, and scope, embeds the prior complete verification only for replacement, and binds both manifest generations into the package identity. M9r recovery conditions pass through with rollback state and retained recovery paths. The contract remains unsigned, non-replayable, and limited to synchronous detected failures under ADR 0057.

M9t adds a host-specific optional-package preflight for the fixed parquet/Arrow and report/Quarto feature rows. It reads bounded installed DESCRIPTION metadata directly without loading either namespace. Missing packages produce skipped_missing_pkg. Arrow is classified against the reviewed 14.0.0 minimum but remains blocked_symbols_unchecked; Quarto remains blocked_version_unpinned. The exact internal evidence binds both rows, observed versions, statuses, reconciled counts, limitations, inspection time, and capability identity while explicitly keeping serialization, rendering, and execution readiness false under ADR 0058 and ADR 0059.

M9u adds the internal fixed Arrow/Parquet serialization substrate. It revalidates one exact harmonized source, derives its redacted typed observation table, then loads Arrow only after safely verifying version 14.0.0 or newer. The loaded namespace version must equal the inspected metadata, and the reviewed write_parquet, read_parquet, and BufferOutputStream exports and formals are resolved immediately. The writer uses an uncompressed Parquet-2.4 profile with dictionaries and statistics disabled, fixed page/buffer/chunk controls, microsecond timestamp coercion, no INT96, and no truncation. Bounded raw bytes must contain both PAR1 markers and read back to the exact typed table in memory. Evidence binds the complete source, table, bytes, version, profile, digest, and identity. Determinism is scoped to one Arrow version; bundle integration, loading, public exposure, writing, and replay remain deferred under ADR 0059.

M9v exposes the fixed profile end to end for harmonized packages. gx_package(..., timeseries = "parquet") serializes the redacted typed observation table to data/observations.parquet, records the Arrow writer and fixed profile in manifest-v1, and uses the same staged verification and owned replacement paths as CSV packages. Catalog and fetched inputs reject Parquet before publication. gx_package_load() recognizes the resource and preserves its exact bytes without Arrow; gx_package_tables() leaves it opaque while parsing the remaining canonical CSVs; and gx_package_hydrate() reads the verified bytes in memory through the reviewed Arrow capability and requires the exact typed observation schema. Cross-Arrow-version byte stability, authenticity, reports, refresh, and replay remain unclaimed under ADR 0060.

M9w adds the internal Quarto R package capability boundary. The bounded M9t preflight now classifies Quarto against a reviewed 1.5.1 minimum while remaining namespace-free and advisory. At operation time, M9w rejects missing or older metadata before loading, requires the loaded namespace version to equal the inspected version, and resolves the reviewed quarto_render(), quarto_path(), quarto_version(), and quarto_available() exports and formals immediately. It invokes none of them, does not locate or run the Quarto CLI, and performs no rendering or filesystem work. CLI admission, a fixed report source and output profile, package integration, and public exposure were deferred under ADR 0061; ADR 0062 now supplies only the separate CLI admission gate, while the report and exposure work remains deferred.

M9x adds the internal Quarto CLI admission boundary. It begins with the exact M9w capability, resolves quarto_path(normalize = TRUE), and requires one normalized existing executable file. Only that exact path is invoked with --version under a five-second timeout. The boundary requires one canonical version value at 1.8.27 or newer and checks the executable’s size, mode, modification time, and change time before and after the command. Exact evidence binds the R package version, CLI path and version, file metadata, command, timeout, limitations, and identity. It does not render, inspect inputs, write report files, authenticate the distribution, or add a public API under ADR 0062.

M9y adds the internal fixed Quarto HTML report boundary. It accepts one exact M9q typed package view and derives only a redacted summary of its stage, hydration identity, and site, dataset, problem, request, fetch, native, observation, and harmonized-resource counts. Those facts enter one bounded, code-free UTF-8 report.qmd with minimal embedded-resource HTML, execution disabled, and cache disabled. The M9x-admitted executable is invoked directly with fixed render arguments and a 30-second timeout, and its filesystem identity must remain unchanged across the command. A private mode-0700 render tree may contain only the unchanged source and report.html. The output is bounded to 8 MiB and parsed without network access; its title, report landmark, identity markers, and all counts must agree, while scripts, frames, objects, embeds, forms, base URLs, refreshes, and external HTTP(S) references are rejected. Exact source and HTML bytes remain in host-specific internal evidence after the owned private tree is removed. Package-resource integration, public exposure, cross-version byte determinism, authenticity, and replay remain unclaimed under ADR 0063.

M9z adds the internal private report-package integration boundary. One exact M9y report is admitted only when its hydrated source package rebinds the stage, timeseries format, package-input identity, bundle identity, and report-free resource profile of one exact M9k base bundle. Every base resource and byte is preserved, and the verified HTML becomes the sole additional report/index.html resource. The report-aware bundle and manifest bind the base bundle, hydration identity, source manifest, source and HTML hashes, Quarto R and CLI versions, resource inventory, counts, and stored bytes. The existing writer stages and verifies this private profile before creation, and M9r applies its same verified sibling-backup rollback to replacement; an intact private report package is itself an admitted replacement owner. Report-free manifest shape and public behavior remain unchanged at that checkpoint. Public loading rejects the private profile and gx_package(..., report = TRUE) remains gated within M9z itself; ADR 0065 later opens those public boundaries. The integration boundary performs no rendering or external work under ADR 0064.

M9aa exposes the reviewed report path publicly. gx_package(report = TRUE) first publishes the exact report-free base bundle to an owned private package, hydrates its fixed typed view, renders through M9y, and integrates through M9z. The private source package remains available while staged and final writer or replacement verification rebind report lineage, then is removed immediately; render failure occurs before the final destination can be created or replaced. Report-bearing packages are admitted by byte loading, canonical table parsing, and typed hydration, with HTML retained as one opaque exact non-table resource. Public gx_report() re-verifies the package, manifest descriptor, HTML digest, and isolated HTML structure without invoking Quarto and either returns the exact bytes in memory or atomically writes them to one absent file. Replacement admits report-free to report, report to report, and report to report-free transitions under the existing sibling-backup rollback. Report-free manifests and default behavior remain unchanged. Authenticity, refresh, replay, Frictionless validation, and cross-Quarto-version byte determinism remain unclaimed under ADR 0065.

M9ab exposes only the offline stored-state branch of gx_replay(). A validated catalog snapshot, public package, loaded package, existing source directory, or its exact manifest.json path is first admitted through complete M9a verification and exact fixed-profile recognition. Catalog snapshots load through M9i; packages load through M9q; a fixed stored report additionally loads through gx_report() without invoking Quarto. The returned gx_replay evidence binds the current manifest, typed view, optional report, source kind, stage, explicit limitations, and deterministic inspection identity. Repeated verification timestamps are excluded only from cross-pass equality; all substantive manifest and resource evidence must agree. refresh = TRUE, a non-NULL destination, nonempty options, arbitrary manifest-v1 profiles, mutation, and evidence forgery fail closed before gaining broader authority. The result is offline, read-only, unsigned, non-Frictionless, and explicitly records both recipe_executed = FALSE and replayable = FALSE. Live recipe refresh and procedural replay remain gated under ADR 0066.

M9ac adds an internal deterministic Frictionless Data Package v1 description over one exact validated M9k/M9z resource bundle. Every descriptor resource is bound to its stored path, byte length, and SHA-256 digest in bundle order. Canonical CSV resources are declared as tabular-data-resource with exact all-string Table Schemas; HTML, Parquet, and other non-CSV bytes are declared explicitly as generic data-resource entries without inferred schemas. The bounded datapackage.json bytes must survive an exact JSON round trip, and construction performs no write, publication, CLI, refresh, or replay work. Python Frictionless CLI 5.19.0 is pinned in a dedicated CI job and validates the catalog, fetched, and harmonized fixed CSV package trees in standards-v1 mode. The in-memory evidence still records cli_validated = FALSE because it does not execute that external runtime. At the M9ac checkpoint, public descriptor integration and CLI acceptance of optional mixed-resource profiles remained gated under ADR 0067.

M9ad exposes the reviewed all-CSV profile through explicit gx_package(..., frictionless = TRUE). It first finalizes the exact base M9k bundle and rejects Parquet, reports, or any non-CSV resource. The descriptor is derived only from those base resources, then added as one generic datapackage.json metadata resource declared by manifest.json; neither metadata file appears in the descriptor’s own resource list. Manifest serialization binds the base bundle, descriptor profile, path, bytes, SHA-256, pinned CLI 5.19.0 profile, and runtime_cli_executed = FALSE. Creation and owned replacement admit descriptor-free to descriptor-bearing and reverse transitions through the existing closed staging and sibling-backup rollback contracts. Offline loading rederives the descriptor from already verified CSV bytes, so a semantically modified descriptor remains rejected even when an unsigned manifest is changed to match its new checksum. Canonical table and typed hydration views leave JSON opaque but preserve frictionless = TRUE; offline stored-state replay inspection preserves the same compatibility evidence without executing a recipe or external runtime. Defaults retain their prior descriptor-free manifest shape. At the M9ad checkpoint, mixed raw/Parquet/report profiles and live procedural replay remained gated under ADR 0068.

M9ae validates those fixed mixed-resource families before any public API expansion. Canonical CSV entries retain exact all-string Table Schemas. Every retained provider body, Arrow/Parquet observation resource, report HTML file, or other non-CSV resource instead uses profile = "data-resource" and format = "bin", so core Frictionless validates it as an opaque file rather than dispatching a semantic format parser. The descriptor still binds the exact path, byte length, SHA-256, and normalized media type; a custom geoconnexr block retains the true extension and validation = "opaque-file-v1". The internal descriptor contract advances to 0.2.0. A dedicated CI case builds real populated-raw, fixed Arrow/Parquet, and verified-report bundles and requires core Python Frictionless CLI 5.19.0 standards-v1 validation to return zero errors and warnings with every opaque resource reported as a file task. This does not install Python format extras, publish mixed descriptors, or authorize refresh or replay under ADR 0069.

M9af completes the fixed-package M9 roadmap by applying the public Frictionless wrapper after each requested fixed bundle is finalized. Retained provider bodies, fixed Arrow/Parquet observations, and verified report HTML therefore publish through the same manifest-bound datapackage.json boundary as canonical CSV packages. Combined manifest recognition preserves the underlying Parquet and report contracts, and verified loading rederives the descriptor from stored mixed resources before table, hydration, report, and offline stored-state inspection proceed. Ordinary operation invokes no Python, default packages remain descriptor-free, and all profiles remain non-replayable. Live refresh and procedural replay remain deferred under ADR 0066 until a complete reproducible request recipe exists; that dependency is not another fixed-package implementation gate.

Frictionless compatibility uses the Python Frictionless CLI in CI; the R frictionless package alone is not treated as comprehensive validation. Profile and non-tabular resources must be declared explicitly.

M9a acceptance: identifier and custom-geometry manifests rebind exact AOI identity; bounded closed-tree checksum verification is deterministic and offline; tampered, missing-required, aliased, undeclared, symlinked, and special entries fail closed; optional absence remains visible; request metadata is described as shape-validated rather than authenticated.

M9b acceptance: empty and populated internal catalogs serialize to four fixed deterministic redacted CSV resources; the exact manifest and resource bytes pass staged and final M9a verification; existing targets and unsafe parents are preserved; pre-publication failures clean owned staging content; post-publication verification failures never recursively delete a possibly replaced target; and no network, discovery, overwrite, or public API is added.

M9c acceptance: the public wrapper returns exact revalidated evidence; resource or manifest projection forgery fails; snapshot bytes remain unchanged; and blocked external-work seams are never invoked.

M9d acceptance: public catalog snapshots serialize through the exact M9b writer and return validated final M9c evidence; malformed catalogs, enabled fetch/report/overwrite flags, forged evidence, metadata, identifiers, and status fail closed; scope rejection occurs before any destination or staging tree is created; and no network or blocked loading/report seam is invoked.

M9e acceptance: empty and populated request exports load to the exact typed request-table schema and round-trip to the manifest ledger; stored bytes are the canonical manifest projection rather than merely a matching hash; unknown profiles, rehashed noncanonical bytes, malformed evidence, mutation, and over-budget resources fail closed; and no external or write seam is invoked.

M9f acceptance: public request-ledger access returns the exact M9e typed table and revalidated evidence; path, row, count, hash, status, and identity forgery fail closed; fixed-profile, byte-binding, mutation, budget, offline, and read-only guarantees are preserved; and no catalog loader or replay API is introduced.

M9g acceptance: empty and populated sites, datasets, and problems CSVs load to exact character tables; parsed tables reproduce the verified bytes; noncanonical encoding, quoting, line endings, headers, or blank lines fail; unknown resources, profile/schema changes, rehashed noncanonical bytes, evidence forgery, mutation, and loading budgets fail closed; and no external or write seam is invoked.

M9h acceptance: empty and populated snapshots produce exact typed redacted site, dataset, problem, and request tables; geometry, time, logical, and JSON fields round-trip their fixed writer encodings; redaction and blank strings remain visible; canonical character data with invalid typed values fails; typed/raw/request/metadata/identity forgery fails closed; and loading remains offline, read-only, internal, and distinct from gx_catalog.

M9i acceptance: public catalog-view loading returns the exact revalidated M9h object; final verification, typed tables, canonical evidence, counts, and identity remain bound; forgery fails closed; print and documentation state that the result is redacted, non-replayable, and not a live gx_catalog; and no external or write seam is invoked.

M9j acceptance: exact catalog, fetched, and harmonized inputs produce distinct validated package-stage objects; fetched/harmonized stages reject a missing or mismatched source catalog; canonical catalog projections, fetched status/results, harmonization determinants, counts, stage, and identity remain bound; native payloads are retained; forgery fails closed; and admission is offline, read-only, internal, and non-serializing.

M9k acceptance: catalog, empty fetched, empty harmonized, and populated harmonized inputs produce exact fixed resource sets; catalog hashes reproduce M9j evidence; retained provider bodies remain byte-identical; no-body direct-CSV results use canonical CSV; every stored length/hash and native-index binding agrees; path, content, resource, metadata, input, or bundle forgery fails closed; and serialization remains bounded, offline, in-memory, write-free, internal, and non-publishing.

M9l acceptance: catalog and harmonized bundles publish exact stored bytes with deterministic package manifests; staged and exposed trees pass M9a and bind the M9k paths, sizes, and hashes; equivalent bundle trees are byte-identical; existing targets survive; injected write, verification, and rename failures clean only the owned stage; post-exposure failure leaves the target untouched; evidence forgery and stored-byte mutation fail closed; and publication remains creation-only, offline, internal, and non-replayable.

M9m acceptance: catalog, fetched, and harmonized inputs publish through the exact M9j–M9l chain and return final verified public evidence; missing or mismatched source catalogs and unsupported format, raw-retention, or overwrite choices fail before publication; existing targets and staging failure semantics remain unchanged; path, stage, verification, metadata, and identity forgery fail closed; creation performs no external work; and serializers, writers, and intermediate evidence remain internal.

M9n acceptance: catalog, fetched, and harmonized packages load only through the fixed M9m writer profile; every returned resource is byte-identical and manifest-bound; non-package snapshots, corruption, replacement, and evidence forgery fail closed; loading performs no external or write work; and the result remains byte-preserving, read-only, unsigned, and non-replayable.

M9o acceptance: catalog, fetched, and harmonized package CSVs parse to path-named character-only tibbles and round-trip to exact M9n bytes; UTF-8 is locale-independent; noncanonical CSV, wrong profiles, corruption, and evidence forgery fail closed; raw resources remain opaque; and no external or write work is performed.

M9p acceptance: catalog, fetched, and harmonized packages hydrate only their fixed package-owned schemas; canonical integer, double, logical, geometry, UTC timestamp, and JSON fields receive exact declared types; request-ledger disagreement, noncanonical scalar text, schema changes, and projection/evidence forgery fail closed; provider-native tables and raw resources remain uninterpreted; hydration remains internal, offline, read-only, redacted, unsigned, and non-replayable; and no external or write work is performed.

M9q acceptance: public gx_package_hydrate() returns the exact revalidated M9p view for catalog, fetched, and harmonized packages; typed projections, canonical evidence, native-table treatment, scope, and identity remain bound; print and documentation state the redacted, read-only, non-replayable, and non-reconstructing scope; forgery fails closed; and no external or write work is performed.

M9r acceptance: replacement admits only an intact fixed-writer package; the replacement fully stages and verifies before the prior tree moves; failed installation or final verification restores and re-verifies the prior package; failed rollback or cleanup retains explicit recovery paths and committed-state evidence; arbitrary or corrupt destinations remain untouched; generation, bundle, metadata, and identity forgery fail closed; the substrate remains internal and offline; and public exposure remains delegated to M9s.

M9s acceptance: public overwrite replaces only an intact fixed-writer package through M9r; creation behavior remains absent-destination-only; replacement results bind prior and final verification, operation metadata, and identity; missing, arbitrary, and corrupt targets remain untouched; detected installation failure restores the prior generation; forgery fails closed; replacement performs no external work; and all replacement internals remain unexported.

M9t acceptance: Arrow and Quarto metadata are inspected through bounded direct reads without namespace loading; missing packages produce explicit skips; Arrow is classified against its reviewed minimum but remains blocked on symbols; Quarto remains version-unpinned; both capability rows, versions, statuses, counts, limitations, timestamp, and identity fail closed; malformed probes fail closed; no serialization, rendering, external, or public API work occurs; and existing M7b preflight behavior remains unchanged.

M9u acceptance: missing or too-old Arrow fails before namespace loading; metadata/namespace races and missing or changed exports fail closed; empty and populated exact typed redacted observations serialize and read back entirely in memory under the fixed profile; repeated writes are byte-identical within one Arrow version; output remains bounded and self-identifying; source, table, byte, metadata, and identity forgery fail closed; no network, filesystem, bundle, loading, report, replay, or public API work occurs; and the existing CSV/raw package profile remains unchanged.

M9v acceptance: exact harmonized inputs publish and replace verified Parquet observation packages under the fixed Arrow profile; catalog/fetched inputs and unknown formats fail before publication; manifests bind the format, writer version, profile, resource dimensions, bytes, and digest; loading is byte-preserving without Arrow; table views leave Parquet opaque; hydration reproduces the exact typed redacted observation schema through Arrow; CSV remains the default; forgery fails closed; and no network, report, refresh, or replay work occurs.

M9w acceptance: missing and too-old Quarto R packages fail before namespace loading; metadata/namespace races and missing or changed exports fail closed; the reviewed render, path, version, and availability functions and formals resolve at 1.5.1 or newer without invocation; M9t reports both reviewed package minimums while remaining namespace-free and advisory; no CLI discovery, execution, rendering, network, filesystem publication, or public API work occurs; and malformed resolver evidence fails under typed Quarto errors.

M9x acceptance: an exact M9w capability plus one normalized unchanged executable reporting Quarto CLI 1.8.27 or newer produces validated host evidence; missing capability, invalid paths, command failure, old or malformed versions, executable races, and forgery fail closed; the exact path and bounded timeout reach the version-command seam; no alternate PATH lookup, render, network, cache, report staging, publication, replay, or public API work occurs.

M9y acceptance: one exact typed package view plus M9x runtime evidence produces a fixed code-free source and bounded minimal HTML with every redacted summary count rebound; the exact admitted path, fixed no-execute/no-cache arguments, and 30-second timeout reach the render seam; active or externally linked HTML, malformed markers, unexpected artifacts, source or CLI mutation, oversized output, render failure, cleanup failure, and evidence forgery fail closed; successful and failed renders remove only their owned private stage; and no network, cache, package publication, manifest mutation, replay, or public API work occurs.

M9z acceptance: one exact M9y report adds one byte-identical HTML resource only to its originating M9k bundle while every base resource remains unchanged; the private manifest binds all base, hydration, source, runtime, HTML, count, and resource evidence; absent-destination creation and owned replacement pass staged and final closed-tree verification; intact report packages can be replaced again; mismatched lineage and bundle, report, byte, resource, manifest, or identity forgery fail closed; report-free manifests remain unchanged; public loading rejects the private profile at the M9z checkpoint; and no rendering, network, cache, refresh, replay, or public API work occurs. ADR 0065 subsequently supersedes that public gate without changing this internal substrate.

M9aa acceptance: explicit public report creation renders only through the reviewed fixed M9y controls, binds one exact HTML resource through M9z, and removes the owned report-free source package only after final lineage verification; report packages load, parse canonical tables, and hydrate while HTML remains opaque exact bytes; gx_report() revalidates the stored digest and isolated structure without Quarto and can atomically copy identical bytes only to an absent file; report-free to report, repeated report, and report to report-free replacements retain prior/final verification and rollback; invalid flags, runtime/render failure, unsafe output, existing output, byte or descriptor mutation, and evidence forgery fail closed; default report-free behavior invokes no report seam and preserves its manifest shape; and authenticity, refresh, replay, and Frictionless claims remain false.

M9ab acceptance: fixed catalog snapshots load as exact M9i typed views; catalog, fetched, harmonized, and report-bearing packages load as exact M9q typed views with optional stored-report evidence; source objects, directories, and exact manifest paths bind the same inspection identity; no network, DNS, cache, writer, optional report runtime, destination, repair, or recipe seam is invoked; refresh, destination, extra options, arbitrary profiles, filesystem mutation, and result forgery fail closed; and the result states its unsigned, read-only, no-execution, and non-replayable limits.

M9ac acceptance: catalog, fetched, and harmonized fixed bundles produce deterministic Data Package v1 descriptors in exact resource-path order; CSV schemas contain the exact stored columns as strings and non-CSV resources are explicitly generic; paths, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes rebind the exact bundle; construction invokes no network, DNS, cache, writer, publication, refresh, or replay seam; descriptor, byte, metadata, and identity forgery fail closed; and the three fixed CSV package stages pass pinned Python Frictionless CLI 5.19.0 standards-v1 validation in CI without errors or warnings.

M9ad acceptance: explicit public all-CSV packages add one exact manifest-declared datapackage.json whose resources rebind every base path, byte length, SHA-256, and canonical string schema without self-reference; default manifests remain descriptor-free; creation and replacement verify the complete tree and admit adding or removing the profile; offline loading rederives descriptor bytes before table, hydration, and stored-state inspection preserve frictionless = TRUE; incompatible options and semantic forgery fail closed; runtime CLI execution remains false; and a publicly generated package passes pinned Python Frictionless CLI 5.19.0 standards-v1 validation.

M9ae acceptance: populated retained-raw, real fixed Arrow/Parquet, and verified-report bundles describe every non-CSV resource as an opaque binary file while retaining its true extension in custom metadata; exact paths, sizes, hashes, and media types remain bound; core pinned Python Frictionless CLI 5.19.0 validates all three profiles with no errors or warnings and reports every opaque resource as a file task; no Python format parser, publication, refresh, or replay boundary is added.

M9af acceptance: public retained-raw, fixed Arrow/Parquet, and verified report packages publish manifest-bound descriptors using the pinned opaque-file profile; combined manifests preserve Parquet, report, and Frictionless evidence; loading rederives mixed descriptors; table, hydration, report, replacement, and stored-state inspection preserve the combined flags without runtime Python or recipe execution; defaults remain descriptor-free; and the fixed-package M9 roadmap is complete.

Deferred beyond the fixed-package M9 roadmap: live refresh and procedural replay require a complete reproducible request recipe under ADR 0066. No additional implementation gate is implied until that dependency exists.

M10 — Publisher tools (post-flagship)

gx_jsonld_build(sites, datasets = NULL, provider, context = gx_context())
gx_jsonld_validate(x)
gx_sitemap(uris, dir)

Builder and validator target an explicit, versioned Geoconnex profile. Location types are validated as IRIs or profile-approved literals based on the P0 evidence; the package must not claim that current production pages uniformly follow a stricter ideal. Validation findings have severity, JSON pointer, rule ID, profile version, and suggested fix.

ADR 0071 implements publisher profile 1.0.0 over the exact catalog 0.1.0 site and dataset contracts. The fixed local context requires no network access. gx_jsonld_build() preserves site, provider, mainstem, point geometry, dataset, distribution, and variable facts in deterministic order. It rejects provider disagreement, unsupported location-type literals, and sparse distribution by variable products before serialization. The accepted literal types are hydrometricStation and Unknown, which are both present in the P0 evidence corpus; canonical location-type IRIs remain preferred.

gx_jsonld_validate() safely expands and parses a candidate, then returns an exact findings table with severity, JSON pointer, stable rule ID, profile version, message, and suggested fix. Errors make the result invalid and warnings do not. gx_sitemap() sorts 1 to 50,000 unique canonical HTTP(S) URIs, emits one deterministic XML file within the 50 MiB protocol ceiling, and publishes only to an absent directory through verified sibling staging. No M10 function performs remote publication or search-engine notification.

M10 acceptance: built profiles round-trip through the existing safe expansion and tolerant parsers; exact publisher facts and supported location types survive; lossy dataset cardinalities fail before serialization; validation reports malformed documents and profile violations as structured findings; sitemap output is deterministic, escaped, count- and byte-bounded, and byte-verified after publication. ADR 0072 supplies the shared installed conformance corpus. R and a Python standard-library harness reproduce its profile, validation-finding, canonical-digest, and sitemap known answers.

6. Data contracts

All contracts include contract_version; exact columns freeze after the P0 vertical slice and P2 provider audit.

6.1 Sites

One row per canonical site_uri: name/type/provider fields, provider ID, mainstem URI, landing URL, typed POINT geometry (empty allowed), primary source, and field-level provenance. Duplicate/cluster relationships are preserved rather than silently collapsed.

6.2 Dataset records

Cardinality is one row per dataset × distribution × variable. Required identifiers:

  • dataset_id: SHA-256 of schema version plus canonical site URI and dataset URI; if no dataset URI exists, use a documented fallback fingerprint of provider URI/name and dataset name;
  • distribution_id: SHA-256 of schema version plus dataset ID, canonical access URL, and media type;
  • variable_id: canonical variable URI, or a namespaced hash of provider and normalized label when unmapped.

Rows also retain dataset_uri, names/descriptions, temporal coverage, variable/unit URIs and labels, distribution URL/media type, provider, licence/access rights, source provenance, classifier result, and fetchability. Hash canonicalization and NA/Unicode handling are specified in a language-neutral JSON document and shared with Python tests.

6.3 Catalog problems and requests

problems records stage/source/code/severity/message/recoverability/time. requests records request identity, stage, method, redacted canonical URL, request hash, final URL, response status/type/bytes/hash, timing, cache origin, and error code. Sensitive query values are redacted from logs and error messages.

6.4 Fetch plan/status

The M7a plan records distribution identity, bound handler metadata, stable selection order, effective time, unplanned parameters, and count/byte budgets. It contains no requests and is explicitly non-executable and non-replayable. The separate M7b report records host package-version capability as advisory state while keeping every implementation blocked and preserving the empty request list. The M7c object records exact inert direct-CSV GET policy, identity, and all-distribution coverage without allocating budgets or authorizing transport. M7d keeps those nested objects byte-identical while reserving global physical-attempt and encoded/decoded-byte capacity for every selected handler and emitting only bounded, non-executable direct-CSV logical request plans. M7e keeps those objects byte-identical while validating one bounded caller- supplied direct-CSV response envelope and raw body without claiming provider origin or budget consumption. M7f keeps that chain byte-identical while parsing the exact retained bytes under a strict bounded UTF-8 profile into an exact character-only schema and table. M7g binds one provider-observed direct-CSV response to an exact physical-attempt ledger row. M7h orchestrates admitted direct-CSV requests sequentially, continues after isolatable transport/parse failures, compacts successful evidence, and reconciles one exact status row for every distribution; its dry run performs no host or provider work. Later M7 contracts build on M7i’s first reservation-bound single-page OGC API Features handler and native invocation-time symbol check. M7j adds shared CSV/OGC admission and global scheduling. M7k adds the first optional-package provider path: one exact WQP Result request, package-owned transport, offline dataRetrieval::importWQP agreement with strict CSV, compact retained evidence, and CSV/WQP/OGC status reconciliation. M7l adds one exact EDR position request, package-owned transport, strict CoverageJSON PointSeries normalization, invocation-time edr4r agreement, and CSV/WQP/EDR/OGC reconciliation. M7m adds one current USGS continuous page, invocation-time dataRetrieval capability validation, package-owned transport, strict string-preserving GeoJSON normalization, and no-follow truncation. M7n adds one current USGS daily page, an exact statistic/local-date contract, Date normalization, conservative missing-match handling, and CSV/WQP/EDR/continuous/daily/OGC reconciliation. ADR 0034 freezes those six families as the supported M7 subset and publishes gx_fetch_plan(), gx_fetch(), and the gx_fetched 0.1.0 result boundary. Remaining provider breadth, pagination, registration, and replay are later enhancements rather than prerequisites for M8. Future result-contract versions may add user-facing elapsed/message fields and fetched times without weakening M7h’s identity, attempt, byte, and one-to-one reconciliation rules.

6.5 Observations

site_uri, dataset_id, distribution_id, variable_id, variable URI/name, UTC datetime, converted value/unit URI/label, original value/unit URI/label, qualifier, harmonized flag, and conversion rule ID. Non-timeseries data keep native shape and are indexed as separate resources.

6.6 Manifest

Publish a JSON Schema under inst/schema/manifest-v1.json. The manifest supports recipe replay and offline resource verification as distinct operations.

7. Non-functional requirements

  • Bounded by default: finite row, page, request, time, encoded-byte, and decoded-byte budgets; unbounded actions require explicit opt-in.
  • Partial failure is visible: recoverable source failures create diagnostics and completeness flags; invalid inputs and broken internal contracts abort.
  • Polite: per-host throttling, maximum concurrency, descriptive user-agent, cache reuse, and bounded live CI.
  • Safe: SSRF and redirect checks, safe schemes, remote-context allowlist, parser-depth/decompression limits, no code execution, and log redaction.
  • Inspectable: request ledger, field provenance, exact asset hashes, handler/template/vocabulary versions.
  • Portable: Windows/macOS/Linux checks; UTF-8 and leading-zero tests; CSV baseline with optional Parquet.

Performance budgets are measured during P0. The former cold/warm HUC8 targets remain goals, not acceptance criteria, until measured against representative provider coverage.

8. Testing, CI, and documentation

8.1 Test layers

  1. pure unit tests with deterministic clock/jitter and no network;
  2. protocol fixtures, minimized and sanitized for package size;
  3. contract tests for every S3 object and zero-row output;
  4. installed-package tests for system.file() assets;
  5. one offline vertical-slice package and checksum verification;
  6. bounded live checks run weekly, skipped on CRAN, with the repository owner assigned through the issue-based notification path in ADR 0073.

Live checks test stable invariants (PID redirects, advertised collection/queryable, bounded SPARQL semantic answer) and record count drift as a diagnostic rather than failing solely because a mutable count changed.

8.2 CI matrix

  • R release, devel, and oldrel on Linux; release on macOS/Windows;
  • R CMD build and R CMD check --as-cran;
  • minimal optional-dependency job;
  • offline/no-network job;
  • lint, exported-API snapshot, JSON Schema validation, and Frictionless CLI validation;
  • scheduled live smoke workflow separate from required PR checks.

8.3 Documentation before 0.1.0

README quickstart, package help, crosswalk and discovery vignettes, cache/offline guide, 200 MB VAA-download notice, optional capability table, error/diagnostics reference, provenance/licensing guide, lifecycle/deprecation policy, CITATION, CONTRIBUTING, security policy, and support expectations.

9. Revised roadmap

Phase Observed state Remaining estimate
P0: decisions and spike Product decisions, safety threat decisions, profiles, mainstem evidence, request plans, and the installed vertical package are complete. Automatic HUC10 graph discovery remains upstream-blocked under ADR 0085. No internal graph estimate
P1: protocol and identity M2 and M3 are implemented. M1 request safety, retries, cache, host throttling, the central scheduler, and internal curl multi transport are implemented. 1 to 2 focused days for public fetch orchestration
P2: crosswalk and discovery M4 is complete through checked composition. The graph root is configurable and experimental; public raw query APIs remain gated. Current merge stack plus the external graph gate
P3a: catalog and package Catalog construction and the fixed offline-verifiable package path are complete. Included in release hardening
P3b: fetch and harmonize The frozen six-handler fetch subset, conservative harmonization, fetched packaging, and HUC10 case study are complete. 1 to 2 focused days per additional named M8 family
P4: report, publisher, and portability Fixed verified reports, M10, and shared R/Python publisher conformance are complete. Included in release hardening
Release hardening Documentation, lifecycle review, and CRAN preparation remain. 2 to 3 focused days

ADR 0087 estimates the unblocked fixed scope at 9 to 14 focused engineering days, plus one aggregate CI matrix per reviewable slice. The current measured matrix allowance is 90 minutes per head revision. Broader M8 work is additive, and the upstream graph capability is excluded from the internal total.

The installed HUC10 case study now records a bounded current-USGS daily fetch, harmonization, Frictionless packaging, closed-tree verification, typed hydration, and offline stored-state inspection. It uses a caller-supplied profile, so the automatic spatial graph discovery portion of the P0 vertical slice remains open.

De-scope in this order: SensorThings, report polish, optional reference layers, mainstem-basin convenience, publisher tools, Python port. Never de-scope contract versioning, diagnostics, request safety, recipe/snapshot distinction, or raw-value preservation.

10. Definition of ready and done

Ready for production implementation

  • P0 gates closed;
  • vertical slice and threat model reviewed;
  • mainstem vintage and SPARQL stability decisions recorded;
  • schemas and handler protocol accepted;
  • dependencies/release channel confirmed.

Done for each module

  • acceptance criteria and contract tests pass;
  • fixtures/evidence cover new network behavior;
  • invalid, empty, missing-package, offline, and partial-failure cases pass;
  • docs and NEWS updated;
  • no undocumented dependencies or raw transport calls;
  • relevant request, schema, security, and migration metadata are preserved.

11. Remaining decisions

No product-owner scope decisions remain open. ADR 0086 keeps administrative layers such as water rights outside the supported 0.x core until a named source completes a separate authority, licence, identity, temporal, and legal semantics review.

ADR 0073 closes live-monitor ownership and response expectations. ADR 0074 closes the graph endpoint decision without exposing a stable raw-query API. ADR 0075 closes the mainstem vintage and migration decision. ADR 0086 closes the administrative-layer scope decision.

The old EDR package-status question and the existence of huc12pp are no longer open. SensorThings is evidence-gated rather than assumed.
